prompt: Which sentence says: Please turn on the light?
en: Please turn on the light.
explain: 把 comes before the thing, then the verb.

en: He washed the fruit clean.
explain: 把 + thing + verb + result.

en: I have put the book in the bag.
explain: 把 + thing + verb + where.

en: Please give this to him.
explain: 把 + thing + verb.

en: He has finished the meal.
explain: 把 and 被 do not go together in one sentence.

prompt: Which sentence says: My cake was eaten by a friend?
en: My cake was eaten by a friend.
explain: 被 comes before the doer.

en: That book was borrowed by him.
explain: thing + 被 + doer + verb.

en: My money was all spent by him.
explain: thing + 被 + doer + verb.

en: The door was closed by the wind.
explain: thing + 被 + doer + verb.

en: The meal was finished by him.
explain: 被 and 把 do not go together; use only one.

prompt: Which sentence says: If the weather is not good, we will watch a film at home?
options: 如果天气不好，我们就在家看电影。
如果天气不好，我们在家就看电影。
zh: 如果天气不好，我们就在家看电影。
en: If the weather is not good, we will watch a film at home.
explain: 就 comes right before the result.

en: If you want to go, tell me.
explain: 如果 + situation, 就 + result.

zh: 你没有时间的话，就明天再来吧。
en: If you do not have time, then come again tomorrow.
explain: 的话 can end the if part.

en: If he does not come, I will leave.
explain: 如果 + situation, 就 + result.

en: If you are tired, rest.
explain: 如果 gives the condition; 就 starts the result.

zh: 他不但会说汉语，而且会写汉字。
en: He can not only speak Chinese but also write characters.
explain: 不但 comes before the first part, 而且 before the second.

zh: 她不但很高，而且很漂亮。
en: She is not only tall but also pretty.
explain: 不但…而且… adds a second quality.

prompt: Which sentence says: This book is not only interesting but also cheap?
options: 这本书不但有意思，而且很便宜。
这本书不但有意思，很便宜而且。
zh: 这本书不但有意思，而且很便宜。
en: This book is not only interesting but also cheap.
explain: 而且 comes at the start of the second part.

zh: 这个房间不但大，而且很干净。
en: This room is not only big but also clean.
explain: 不但 + A, 而且 + B.

en: He is not only clever but also hardworking.
explain: 不但 + A, 而且 + B.

zh: 他不但喜欢运动，而且喜欢看书。
en: He not only likes sport but also likes reading.
wrong: 他不但喜欢运动，但是而且喜欢看书。
explain: 而且 already adds a point; do not add 但是 (but).

en: I am tired, but I do not want to rest.
explain: 可是 shows a contrast: tired, but still no rest.

prompt: Which sentence says: I very much want to go, but I am too busy today?
options: 我很想去，可是今天太忙了。
我很想去，今天太忙了可是。
zh: 我很想去，可是今天太忙了。
en: I very much want to go, but I am too busy today.
explain: 可是 starts the second part.

en: He ate, and then went to work.
explain: 然后 means and then.

zh: 这个菜很好吃，而且很便宜。
en: This dish is tasty, and it is cheap too.
explain: 而且 adds a second good point.

en: I want to go, but I have no money.
wrong: 我想去，可是但是没有钱。
explain: 可是 already means but; do not add 但是.

zh: 只要有时间，我就去看你。
en: As long as I have time, I will come and see you.
explain: 只要 gives the condition, 就 gives the result.

prompt: Which sentence says: As long as you come, I am happy?
en: As long as you come, I am happy.
explain: 只要 goes with 就. 才 goes with 只有.

prompt: Which sentence says: As long as you rest well, you will get better?
options: 只要你好好休息，就会好的。
只要你好好休息，会好的就。
zh: 只要你好好休息，就会好的。
en: As long as you rest well, you will get better.
explain: 就 comes right before the result.

zh: 只要明天不下雨，我们就去公园。
en: As long as it does not rain tomorrow, we will go to the park.
explain: 只要 + condition, 就 + result.

en: As long as he has money, he buys.
explain: 只要 + condition, 就 + result.

en: As long as you agree, I will do it.
explain: 只要…就… goes with 就; do not use 才 here.

en: I will go only if you go.
explain: 只有 goes with 才, never 就.

prompt: Which sentence says: Only by listening a lot can one understand?
en: Only by listening a lot can one understand.
explain: 才 comes before the result verb.

zh: 只有等到明天，我才有时间。
en: Only by waiting until tomorrow will I have time.
explain: 只有 + condition, 才 + result.

zh: 只有天晴，我们才出去玩。
en: Only if it is sunny will we go out to play.
explain: 只有 + condition, 才 + result.

en: Only by train can I go.
wrong: 只有坐火车，我就才能去。
explain: 只有…才… goes with 才; do not use 就 here.

prompt: Which sentence says: Except for Saturday, I go to work every day?
options: 除了星期六，我每天都上班。
除了星期六，我每天上班都。
zh: 除了星期六，我每天都上班。
en: Except for Saturday, I go to work every day.
explain: 都 comes before the verb.

en: Besides fish, I also want eggs.
explain: 除了 + A, 还 + B means besides.

en: Except me, no one came.
explain: 除了 + the exception, then 都.

zh: 除了看电视，他还喜欢听音乐。
en: Besides watching TV, he also likes listening to music.
explain: 除了 + A, 还 + B.

en: Except him, we all went.
explain: 除了 already marks the exception; do not add 只.

en: He gets up early in order to study.
explain: 为了 + purpose goes at the start.

zh: 为了看电影，我们去了电影院。
en: In order to see a film, we went to the cinema.
explain: 为了 gives the reason for doing it.

prompt: Which sentence says: In order to see Mom, I went home?
en: In order to see Mom, I went home.
explain: 为了 comes first, before the purpose.

prompt: Which sentence says: For the sake of good health, he runs every day?
options: 为了身体好，他每天跑步。
为了他每天跑步，身体好。
zh: 为了身体好，他每天跑步。
en: For the sake of good health, he runs every day.
explain: 为了 + purpose comes first.

zh: 为了买这本书，我走了很远。
en: In order to buy this book, I walked a long way.
explain: 为了 + purpose.

zh: 为了考试，他每天都学习。
en: For the exam, he studies every day.
explain: 为了 + purpose, then what is done.

zh: 为了家人，她很努力工作。
en: For her family, she works very hard.
wrong: 为了因为家人，她很努力工作。
explain: 为了 gives the purpose; do not add 因为 (because).

zh: 他为朋友买了一个手机。
en: He bought a phone for his friend.
explain: 为 + person comes before the verb.

en: Mom cooked many dishes for me.
explain: 为 + person says who it is done for.

prompt: Which sentence says: She bought a lot of fruit for us?
options: 她为我们买了很多水果。
她买了很多水果为我们。
zh: 她为我们买了很多水果。
en: She bought a lot of fruit for us.
explain: 为 + person goes before the verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: Dad prepared lunch for us?
options: 爸爸为我们准备了午饭。
爸爸准备了为我们午饭。
zh: 爸爸为我们准备了午饭。
en: Dad prepared lunch for us.
explain: 为 + person comes before the verb.

en: I bought a present for you.
explain: 为 + person + verb.

en: He sang for everyone.
explain: 为 + person + verb.

en: Mom made a cake for me.
explain: 为 and 给 both point to the person; use only one.

zh: 我想看一本关于中国的书。
en: I want to read a book about China.
explain: 关于 + topic + 的 describes the noun.

zh: 这是一本关于音乐的书。
en: This is a book about music.
explain: 关于 + topic + 的 comes before the noun.

prompt: Which sentence says: This is a film about travelling?
en: This is a film about travelling.
explain: 关于 comes before the topic.

zh: 关于这个问题，我不太清楚。
en: I am not too sure about this question.
explain: 关于 + topic.

zh: 我有关于这件事的问题。
en: I have a question about this matter.
explain: 关于 + topic + 的 + noun.

zh: 这是一本关于历史的书。
en: This is a book about history.
wrong: 这是一本关于讲历史的书。
explain: 关于 is followed by the topic itself, not a verb.

zh: 根据这张地图，银行就在前面。
en: According to this map, the bank is just ahead.
explain: 根据 + source starts the sentence.

zh: 根据老师说的，明天不考试。
en: According to what the teacher says, there is no test tomorrow.
explain: 根据 introduces where the information comes from.

prompt: Which sentence says: According to the map, we go right?
en: According to the map, we go right.
explain: 根据 comes before what it is based on.

prompt: Which sentence says: According to what he says, this is cheap?
options: 根据他说的，这个很便宜。
他说的根据，这个很便宜。
zh: 根据他说的，这个很便宜。
en: According to what he says, this is cheap.
explain: 根据 comes before the source.

zh: 根据医生说的，你要多休息。
en: According to what the doctor says, you must rest more.
explain: 根据 + source, then what follows.

en: According to the map, we have gone the wrong way.
explain: 根据 + source, then what follows.

zh: 根据他的电话，他已经到了。
en: According to his call, he has already arrived.
wrong: 根据从他的电话，他已经到了。
explain: 根据 means according to; do not add 从.

prompt: Which sentence says: Do you drink tea or coffee??
en: Do you drink tea or coffee?
explain: In a question, use 还是.

zh: 星期六或者星期天，我都可以去。
en: Saturday or Sunday, I can go either day.
explain: 或者 gives a choice in a statement.

zh: 你想走路去，还是坐出租车去？
en: Do you want to walk there, or take a taxi?
explain: 还是 asks which one.

zh: 你们坐飞机还是坐火车？
en: Are you going by plane or by train?
explain: 还是 asks which one.

en: Do you want water or milk?
wrong: 你想喝水还是或者牛奶？
explain: In a question, use 还是 alone; do not add 或者.

en: Drink water first, then eat.
explain: 再 comes before the second action.

prompt: Which sentence says: Do homework first, then watch TV?
en: Do homework first, then watch TV.
explain: 再 comes before the second action.

en: I will eat breakfast first, then go to work.
explain: 先 + first action, 再 + second action.

en: He buys a ticket first, then goes in.
explain: 先 + first action, 再 + second action.

en: First take the train, then the plane.
explain: 先 comes first, then 再 for the next step.

zh: 她一边听音乐，一边做作业。
en: She does homework while listening to music.
explain: One 一边 before each action.

zh: 我们一边走路，一边说话。
en: We talk while walking.
explain: 一边…一边… joins two actions at the same time.

prompt: Which sentence says: He talks while drinking tea?
en: He talks while drinking tea.
explain: Each 一边 goes before its verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: She listens to music while cooking?
options: 她一边做饭，一边听音乐。
她一边做饭，听音乐一边。
zh: 她一边做饭，一边听音乐。
en: She listens to music while cooking.
explain: 一边 comes before each verb.

en: I sing while taking a shower.
explain: 一边 + action, 一边 + action.

en: He looks at his phone while walking.
explain: 一边 + action, 一边 + action.

en: I read while eating.
wrong: 我一边吃饭，才一边看书。
explain: 一边…一边… joins two actions at the same time; do not add 才.

en: This room is both big and pretty.
explain: 又…又… joins two qualities.

en: This phone is both good and cheap.
explain: 又 goes before each quality.

en: She is both tall and pretty.
explain: 又…又… already describes the degree, so no 很.

prompt: Which sentence says: This piece of clothing is both nice-looking and cheap?
options: 这件衣服又好看又便宜。
这件衣服又好看便宜又。
zh: 这件衣服又好看又便宜。
en: This piece of clothing is both nice-looking and cheap.
explain: 又 comes before each quality.

en: He is both tired and hungry.
explain: 又 + quality, 又 + quality.

en: This place is both far and dear.
explain: 又 + quality, 又 + quality.

en: She is both clever and pretty.
explain: Do not put 很 after 又.

prompt: Which sentence says: I watched that film again yesterday?
options: 我昨天又看了那个电影。
我昨天再看了那个电影。
zh: 我昨天又看了那个电影。
en: I watched that film again yesterday.
explain: For something that already happened again, use 又.

en: I will call you again tomorrow.
explain: 再 is for something that has not happened yet.

en: I want to watch it once more.
explain: 再 + verb.

en: He forgot to bring his phone again.
explain: 又 is for something that already happened again.

en: We will see each other again tomorrow.
explain: For something that has not happened yet, use 再, not 又.

en: The more he talks, the faster he goes.
explain: 越 goes before each verb or adjective.

en: The more I study, the more I like Chinese.
explain: 越…越… shows two things growing together.

prompt: Which sentence says: The more I study, the happier I am?
en: The more I study, the happier I am.
explain: Use 越 twice, not 越 and 很.

prompt: Which sentence says: The more he runs, the faster he gets?
en: The more he runs, the faster he gets.
explain: 越 comes before each verb or quality.

en: The snow falls harder and harder.
explain: 越 + verb, 越 + quality.

en: The more he thinks, the angrier he gets.
explain: 越 + verb, 越 + quality.

en: The more I study, the more I like it.
explain: Do not put 很 after the second 越.

prompt: Which sentence says: I have more and more friends?
en: I have more and more friends.
explain: The word is 越来越, in that order.

en: His Chinese is getting better and better.
explain: 越来越 + quality shows a steady change.

en: I like it here more and more.
explain: 越来越 comes before the verb.

en: The weather gets hotter and hotter.
explain: Do not put 很 after 越来越.

en: He did not eat until twelve.
explain: 才 shows it happened later than expected.

prompt: Which sentence says: He did not come until nine?
en: He did not come until nine.
explain: 才 means later than expected. 就 means earlier.

prompt: Which sentence says: He does not get home until ten in the evening?
en: He does not get home until ten in the evening.
explain: 才 comes after the time, before the verb.

en: I did not go to bed until twelve yesterday.
explain: time + 才 + verb means late.

en: He does not eat lunch until three.
explain: time + 才 + verb means late.

en: He does not get up until nine.
explain: 才 and 就 are opposites; do not use both.

en: We were already there at six.
explain: 就 comes before the verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: He was at school as early as seven?
en: He was at school as early as seven.
explain: For early, use 就.

en: We got up as early as five.
explain: time + 就 + verb means early.

en: She went out as early as six.
explain: time + 就 + verb means early.

en: He had already left at eight.
explain: 就 and 才 are opposites; do not use both.

en: I have just bought a phone.
explain: 刚 comes right before the verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: I have just finished eating?
en: I have just finished eating.
explain: 刚 comes before the verb.

en: She has just got off work.
explain: 刚 + verb means just.

en: We have just arrived.
explain: 刚刚 comes before the verb.

en: He has just left.
explain: 刚 already means just; do not add 刚才.

en: Where were you just now?
explain: 刚才 can start the sentence.

en: What did you say just now?
explain: 刚才 means a moment ago.

prompt: Which sentence says: Who came just now??
en: Who came just now?
explain: 刚才 is a time word; it comes first or before the verb.

en: I was taking a shower just now.
explain: 刚才 means just now.

en: Where did he go just now?
explain: 刚才 + the question.

en: I saw him just now.
explain: 看见 is a result verb; do not put 在 before it.

en: He has been at home all along.
explain: 一直 means all the time, without stopping.

en: I have always liked Chinese.
explain: 一直 comes before the verb or adjective.

prompt: Which sentence says: The weather has been cold all along?
en: The weather has been cold all along.
explain: 一直 comes before the verb or quality.

en: He has been waiting for you all along.
explain: 一直 means all along.

en: We keep walking and do not rest.
explain: 一直 comes before the verb.

en: I have always lived here.
explain: 一直 already means all along; do not add 常常 (often).

en: She is always happy.
explain: 总是 means always.

prompt: Which sentence says: He is always at home?
en: He is always at home.
explain: 总是 goes before 在.

prompt: Which sentence says: I always forget his name?
en: I always forget his name.
explain: 老是 comes before the verb.

en: I always take the metro to work.
explain: 总是 means always.

en: He is always the first to arrive.
explain: 总是 comes before the verb.

en: He always gets home very late.
wrong: 他老是常常很晚才回家。
explain: 老是 already means always; do not add 常常.

en: I usually get up at eight.
explain: 平时 means usually.

en: We often go to that restaurant.
explain: 常常 goes before the verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: He often watches films?
en: He often watches films.
explain: 常常 goes before the verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: I usually do not drink coffee?
en: I usually do not drink coffee.
explain: 平时 comes before 不.

en: He often calls me.
explain: 常常 means often.

en: I usually eat breakfast at seven.
explain: 一般 means usually.

en: We often go to the park.
explain: 常常 means often; do not add 总是 (always).

prompt: Which sentence says: Today is even colder than yesterday?
en: Today is even colder than yesterday.
explain: 更 comes right before the quality word.

en: This dish is extremely tasty.
explain: quality + 极了 means extremely.

en: This piece of clothing is quite pretty.
explain: 挺 + quality + 的 means quite.

en: I rather like this one.
explain: 比较 comes before the verb.

en: This room is quite big.
explain: 挺 already means quite; do not add 很.

en: My phone is the same as yours.
explain: A 跟 B 一样.

en: These two cups are the same size.
explain: 一样 + adjective says they are equal.

prompt: Which sentence says: I am the same age as him?
en: I am the same age as him.
explain: A 跟 B 一样 + quality.

zh: 他的手机跟我的不一样。
en: His phone is not the same as mine.
explain: A 跟 B 一样 or 不一样.

en: His name is the same as mine.
explain: A 跟 B 一样.

en: These two characters are different.
explain: 不同 and 不一样 both mean different; use only one.

en: Today is even hotter than yesterday.
explain: 比 + 更 means even more.

prompt: Which sentence says: My older brother is much taller than me?
en: My older brother is much taller than me.
explain: 比 comes before the person you compare with.

en: This one is even more expensive than that one.
explain: 比 + thing + 还 + quality.

en: He is 2 years older than me.
explain: A 比 B + quality + amount.

en: Today is much colder than yesterday.
explain: Do not put 很 in a 比 sentence.

prompt: Which sentence says: This question is hard to answer?
en: This question is hard to answer.
explain: 难 comes before the verb.

en: In summer, food goes bad easily.
explain: 容易 + verb means easy to.

en: This character is hard to read.
explain: 难 + verb means hard to.

en: This phone is easy to use.
explain: 容易 + verb.

en: Chinese is not easy to learn.
explain: 不 goes right before 容易.

prompt: Which sentence says: He speaks very clearly?
en: He speaks very clearly.
explain: verb + 得 + quality.

en: I cannot write this character well.
explain: verb + 不 + result means cannot.

en: There is no room for all of us to sit.
explain: verb + 不 + result.

en: She sings very pleasantly.
explain: verb + 得 + how well.

en: I cannot get a ticket.
explain: 不 goes right between the verb and the result.

prompt: Which sentence says: He walked out of the house?
en: He walked out of the house.
explain: verb + 出来 means out toward the speaker.

en: Everyone stood up.
explain: 起来 after a verb shows the start of an action or going up.

en: He has walked back.
explain: verb + 回来.

en: Everyone sat down.
explain: 下来 already gives the direction; do not add 去.

en: He walks toward me.
explain: 向 + person goes before the verb.

en: Please walk forward.
explain: 向 + direction goes before the verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: He walked toward me?
en: He walked toward me.
explain: 向 + person comes before the verb.

prompt: Which sentence says: Please go to the right?
en: Please go to the right.
explain: 向 + direction comes before the verb.

en: He borrowed money from me.
explain: 向 + person + verb.

zh: 我向老师问了一个问题。
en: I asked the teacher a question.
explain: 向 + person + verb.

en: He said goodbye to his friend.
explain: 向 already points to the person; do not add 给.

en: I watched TV for an hour.
explain: 了 goes right after the verb, before the length of time.

prompt: Which sentence says: I slept for 8 hours?
en: I slept for 8 hours.
explain: verb + 了 + duration.

en: We played for an afternoon.
explain: verb + 了 + duration.

en: She studied Chinese for 3 years.
explain: verb + 了 + duration + thing.

en: He waited for 2 hours.
explain: 了 marks the finished action; do not add 过 here.

en: I have not eaten for two days.
explain: Length of time + 没 + verb + 了.

prompt: Which sentence says: I have not seen him for a year?
en: I have not seen him for a year.
explain: The time comes before 没.

prompt: Which sentence says: I have not taken a shower for 3 days?
en: I have not taken a shower for 3 days.
explain: duration comes before 没.

en: He has not been home for 2 years.
explain: duration + 没 + verb + 了.

zh: 我们一个星期没见面了。
en: We have not met for a week.
explain: duration + 没 + verb + 了.

en: I have not seen a film for a month.
wrong: 我一个月才没看电影了。
explain: Do not add 才; 没 … 了 says how long something has not happened.

prompt: Which sentence says: Before going to bed, I will wash my hands?
en: Before going to bed, I will wash my hands.
explain: 以前 comes right after the action.

zh: 来中国以前，他不会说汉语。
en: Before coming to China, he could not speak Chinese.
explain: action + 以前 means before.

en: After class, we go to eat.
explain: action + 以后 means after.

en: Three years ago, I lived here.
wrong: 三年以前，我住在这里以后。
explain: Use 以前 or 以后, not both.

en: He eats first, then goes to school.
explain: 然后 starts the second action.

zh: 我先去了商店，后来去了医院。
en: I went to the shop first, and later to the hospital.
